stories.title: Iran and Qatar discuss two-day plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz as US-Iran mediation continues
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran and Qatar are discussing a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days and restart peace talks, if Washington meets Tehran's conditions, which include lifting recent US sanctions and reinstating June oil waivers. President Trump said talks were going fine but not very reliable, and that some Iranian targets still need to be dealt with. Euronews reported that Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered commanders to prepare for possible new US-Israeli action, and several outlets report that renewed strikes are seen as more likely after the US midterms on November 3. Qatar and Pakistan are the mediators; a June memorandum of understanding collapsed in August.

stories.title: US midterms enter final weekend with several Senate races close
stories.summary: With the midterm elections on Tuesday, November 3, candidates campaigned across battleground states over the weekend. A Fox News poll showed Maine's Senate race tied at 49-49 between Sen. Susan Collins and Democrat Troy Jackson. Ohio early voting reached 1,485,900 ballots as of Saturday morning per the Associated Press, above the 2022 midterm record of 1,473,983. Other closely watched Senate contests include Alaska, Texas, Michigan and Kansas.

stories.title: Binance reopens withdrawals in phases after $6.3 billion hack
stories.summary: Binance began reopening withdrawals on Sunday, starting with bitcoin, ether, USDT, USDC, BNB and XRP, after what it estimates was a $6.3 billion theft from its hot wallets late Thursday. The exchange says it has replaced about 95% of affected assets with company funds, up from 90% a day earlier, and will absorb the losses rather than pass them to users. About $3 billion is reported frozen, mostly stablecoins. Analytics firms attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korea-linked group, and Binance has promised a full proof-of-reserves report.

stories.title: Flaw in ChatGPT shared links could have run attacker code in signed-in sessions
stories.summary: Security firm Parameter reported that a malicious shared ChatGPT link could run attacker code in a victim's signed-in session and read private conversations. The flaw stemmed from the MathLive library acting on a settings message without checking its sender, allowing injected HTML to create an unsandboxed frame. It was reported on October 18 and OpenAI raised it to P1; by October 26 two versions of the web frontend rejected the messages involved. Parameter reports no real-world exploitation, no user action is needed, and OpenAI paid a $5,000 bounty.

stories.title: Johns Hopkins team identifies receptor used by a colon-cancer-linked bacterial toxin
stories.summary: Researchers at Johns Hopkins reported in Nature that a toxin from certain Bacteroides fragilis strains, found in the gut of up to 20% of healthy people, docks onto the protein claudin-4 on colon cells before damaging E-cadherin. A genome-wide CRISPR screen found that disabling the claudin-4 gene blocked toxin binding. A soluble claudin-4-based decoy protected mice from tissue damage. The mouse data show protection from damage, not prevention of colorectal cancer, and the structure of the toxin-receptor complex is not yet resolved.

stories.title: Study of Shanidar Cave Neanderthal suggests lethal spear wound and funerary behaviour
stories.summary: University of Cambridge researchers report in Scientific Reports that a Neanderthal who died about 75,000 years ago at Shanidar Cave in Iraqi Kurdistan had a 15 mm circular hole in the left shoulder blade, likely made by a sharpened wooden spear and possibly a deliberate heart shot. The individual also had a split lower incisor and survived at least a year with the injury, which the authors argue implies care from others. The remains were among five individuals found in a confined space about 1.5 by 1 by 1 meters, which the researchers interpret as evidence of funerary behaviour.
